items.informal_name: Additivity of Weight Under Subtraction of a Single Element
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {w : σ → M} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] {f : σ →₀ ℕ} {i : σ},
  f i ≠ 0 → (Finsupp.weight w) (f - Finsupp.single i 1) + w i = (Finsupp.weight w) f
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $ and index $ i \in \sigma $ with $ f(i) \neq 0 $, the weight of $ f - \delta_i $ (where $ \delta_i $ denotes the function taking value 1 at $ i $ and 0 elsewhere) satisfies $ \text{weight}_w(f - \delta_i) + w(i) = \text{weight}_w(f) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Weighted Vector Subtraction with Set Mapping under Embedding
items.type:
∀ {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [inst : Ring k] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module k V]
  [S : AddTorsor V P] {ι : Type u_4} {ι₂ : Type u_5} (s₂ : Finset ι₂) (e : ι₂ ↪ ι) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P),
  ((Finset.map e s₂).weightedVSub p) w = (s₂.weightedVSub (p ∘ ⇑e)) (w ∘ ⇑e)
items.informal_description: For an injective function $ e : \iota_2 \to \iota $, a finite set $ s_2 $, a weight function $ w : \iota \to k $, and a point function $ p : \iota \to P $ in an affine space over a field $ k $, the weighted vector subtraction over the image $ s_2.map(e) $ satisfies $ \operatorname{weightedVSub}_{s_2.map(e)}(p, w) = \operatorname{weightedVSub}_{s_2}(p \circ e, w \circ e) $. This expresses that applying the weighted subtraction after mapping the set via $ e $ is equivalent to composing the weight and point functions with $ e $ before applying the subtraction.

items.informal_name: Existence of Injective Linear Map from Finite Support Functions Given Injective Map on Finite Sequences
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {P : Type u_4} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid P] [inst_2 : Module R P] {n : ℕ}
  {f : (Fin (n + 1) → P) →ₗ[R] Fin n → P}, Function.Injective ⇑f → ∃ g, Function.Injective ⇑g
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $ and $ R $-module $ P $, if there exists an injective linear map from the space of functions $ \text{Fin}(n+1) \to P $ to $ \text{Fin}(n) \to P $, then there exists an injective linear map from the space of finite support functions $ \mathbb{N} \to_0 P $ to $ \text{Fin}(n) \to P $.

items.informal_name: Linear Combination Commutes with Domain Mapping
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] {α' : Type u_7} {M' : Type u_8} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M']
  [inst_2 : Module R M'] {v' : α' → M'} (f : α → α') (l : α →₀ R),
  (Finsupp.linearCombination R v') (Finsupp.mapDomain f l) = (Finsupp.linearCombination R (v' ∘ f)) l
items.informal_description: For a function $ f : \alpha \to \alpha' $ and a finite support function $ l : \alpha \to_0 R $, the linear combination of the domain-mapped function $ \text{mapDomain } f \, l $ with vectors $ v' : \alpha' \to M $ equals the linear combination of $ l $ with the composed vectors $ v' \circ f $. Formally, $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)} (\text{mapDomain } f \, l)(i) \cdot v'(i) = \sum_{i \in \text{support } l} l(i) \cdot v'(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Weighted Vector Subtraction with Embedding of Finite Sets
items.type:
∀ {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {P : Type u_3} [inst : Ring k] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_2 : Module k V]
  [S : AddTorsor V P] {ι : Type u_4} {ι₂ : Type u_5} (s₂ : Finset ι₂) (e : ι₂ ↪ ι) (w : ι → k) (p : ι → P) (b : P),
  ((Finset.map e s₂).weightedVSubOfPoint p b) w = (s₂.weightedVSubOfPoint (p ∘ ⇑e) b) (w ∘ ⇑e)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s_2 $ in $ \iota_2 $, an injective function $ e : \iota_2 \to \iota $, scalar weights $ w : \iota \to k $, points $ p : \iota \to P $ in an affine space $ P $, and a base point $ b \in P $, the weighted vector subtraction from $ b $ applied to the image of $ s_2 $ under $ e $ equals the weighted vector subtraction from $ b $ applied directly to $ s_2 $ with $ p $ and $ w $ composed with $ e $. Formally, $ \sum_{i \in s_2} w(e(i)) \cdot (p(e(i)) - b) = \sum_{i \in s_2} (w \circ e)(i) \cdot ((p \circ e)(i) - b) $.
